# Copilot instructions for rtd-calibration-ana

Quick, actionable guidance to help an AI coding agent become productive in this repo.

- Purpose: RTD calibration analysis. Core code is under `RTD_Calibration_VGP/src/`. Data (logfile and example temperature files) are under `RTD_Calibration_VGP/data/` (see `LogFile.csv` and `temperature_files/CalSetN_1/smoke_run_*.txt`).

- High-level architecture (what to read first):
  - `src/run.py` — per-run loader and plotting. Key methods: `Run.load_temperature_file()`, `Run.associate_sensors()`, `Run.filter_faulty_channels()`, `Run.read_run_info()`.
  - `src/set.py` — groups runs by `CalibSetNumber`, computes offsets/repeatability, and picks reference sensors using project-specific maps (`discarded_sensors`, `sensors_raised_by_set`).
  - `src/logfile.py` — wrapper around the CSV `LogFile.csv`; used to look up filenames, sensor columns (`S1`..`S20`) and run metadata.
  - Other helpers: `calibration_network.py`, `runSTS.py`, `setSTS.py` implement alternate analyses; scan them for domain-specific logic.

- Data expectations and examples:
  - `LogFile.csv` (and `LogFile_smoke.csv`) must include: `Filename`, `Selection`, `CalibSetNumber`, `Date`, `N_Run`, and sensor columns named `S1`..`S20` (or similar). `Run.associate_sensors()` maps `S1..S20` -> `channel_1..channel_14`.
  - Temperature files: plain text, tab-separated, no header. After load the DataFrame should have `Date`, `Time`, `channel_1`..`channel_14`.
  - Example smoke data is in `RTD_Calibration_VGP/data/temperature_files/CalSetN_1/`.

- Project-specific conventions (do not change silently):
  - Sensor IDs are handled as integers (code often uses int(float(val))). Keep this tolerant parsing when editing logfile-related code.
  - Many functions return pandas DataFrames; preserve those signatures. Visualizations are generated by Run/Set methods and notebooks expect DataFrame outputs.
  - `Set.group_runs_by_set()` filters out filenames containing `pre`, `st`, `lar` and rows where `Selection == 'BAD'`. The per-set dictionaries (`discarded_sensors`, `sensors_raised_by_set`) are authoritative—edit them rather than changing selection logic.
  - `Run.load_temperature_file()` searches only in local `data/temperature_files/` (recursively). All data files must be placed there.

- Developer workflows & quick commands:
  - Install deps: `pip install -r requirements.txt` or editable install `pip install -e .` (project has `setup.py`).
  - Run tests: `pytest -q` (there are tests under `tests/` covering config and set behavior).
  - Interactive exploration: use notebooks in `/notebooks/` (e.g. `RUN.ipynb`, `SET_BUENO.ipynb`) which demonstrate typical processing flows.

- Integration points & runtime assumptions:
  - Data files are loaded from local `RTD_Calibration_VGP/data/temperature_files/` directory (recursively). No external dependencies like CERNBox.
  - Configuration lives in `RTD_Calibration_VGP/config.yml` and `RTD_Calibration_VGP/config/` (see `sensors.yaml`, `tree.yaml`). Use these for mapping sensor metadata.

- Where to look for changes and examples:
  - `RTD_Calibration_VGP/src/run.py` — temperature parsing, timezone/date handling, column renaming to sensor IDs.
  - `RTD_Calibration_VGP/src/set.py` — grouping and offset calculation; shows how references are chosen.
  - `RTD_Calibration_VGP/src/logfile.py` — illustrates the tolerant parsing of sensor ID columns.
  - Notebooks in `/notebooks/` show end-to-end examples and are useful for integration tests.

- Small safety checklist when editing:
  - Run `pytest` after changes.
  - If you change CSV/column expectations, update notebooks and `tests/` accordingly.
  - Preserve DataFrame-based APIs and sensor ID typing.

If you want, I can shorten or expand any section, add an example LogFile header, or create a tiny smoke test that demonstrates `Run.load_temperature_file()` with the sample `smoke_run_*.txt` files.
